summary.headline: NOCIL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 403 crore and EBITDA margin hit 11.2%, but volumes fell 3% QoQ on supply constraints.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 403 crore, up 20% YoY and 22% QoQ, with volumes up 9% YoY but down 3% QoQ. Management attributed the sequential volume dip to utility and logistics constraints linked to the geopolitical situation, which pushed some orders into later quarters. EBITDA rose to Rs 45 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT to Rs 28 crore, though management described several conversion-cost items as one-offs. Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) was approved on 20 June 2026, while the Pilflex 13 duty awaits Government approval. FY27 guidance was set at revenue of Rs 1,400-1,600 crore and EBITDA around 10%.

segments.name: Tyre chemicals (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew double digits YoY, supported by GST 2.0 and healthy tyre replacement and OEM demand. Management said the 9% volume growth skewed towards tyres.

segments.name: Non-tyre chemicals
segments.commentary: Temporary demand contraction in the quarter from lower production at smaller customers due to input cost spikes, contract labour shortages and LPG shortages. Management expects recovery.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export volumes grew single digits YoY on conversion of ongoing customer engagements. Exports were about 33% of Q1 volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 1,400-1,600 crore, based on current pricing environment.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 10%, with some quarterly adjustments expected.
FY27 volume growth assumed at around 10% YoY; management said it has not scaled this down.
Management expects deferred volumes to be recovered in coming quarters.
Realisations expected to moderate from Q1 levels, though not all of the price gains will reverse.

TDQ plant at Dahej: first revenues expected this year, starting with non-tyre customers, with tyre approvals following over the next couple of quarters. Management expects volumes to start trickling in Q4 FY27 and to build more in Q1 FY28.
Export share expected to rise towards 40-45% by FY28-29 (directional).
capex_capacity: New TDQ plant at Dahej in trial production with samples sent to customers; approval cycle typically 6-8 months, sometimes shorter.
Rs 130 crore investment at Dahej progressing on schedule despite war-related disruption.
Specialty segment expansion is expected to add at least 5-10% to the top line over one to two years, from the current ~15% share (per management).
demand_pricing: Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) notified 20 June 2026; no realisation gain booked in Q1 as the effect depends on how much importers absorb.
DGTR issued a positive final recommendation on Pilflex 13 in June 2026; the Central Government decision is pending, with an outcome expected around end-September.
ADD-covered product lines are about 25-30% of top line excluding TDQ, if Pilflex 13 is also imposed (per management).

Realisation growth implied by guidance is about 30-40%, driven by price increases, product mix, better domestic accelerator pricing and operating leverage. Management flagged moderation from Q1 levels.

Antioxidant imports and dumping remain a concern; management said import influx has not risen significantly after the ADD changes. Chinese yuan and INR movements have had no significant impact so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA run rate sustainable, and what are the one-off conversion cost items?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to around 10% EBITDA for FY27. Conversion cost rose from Rs 110 crore to Rs 130 crore QoQ due to freight, CSR spend, utility cost from gas constraints, plant maintenance, and a Rs 45 crore stock change. Management called some items one-offs, quantified only as 'a few crores' of maintenance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 volume growth guidance (around 10%) below expectations of double-digit export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been mainly in non-tyre and not in tyre, and it has not cut the 10% FY27 volume growth outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ADD benefit will flow to EBITDA, and what is the inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to quantify the ADD benefit. It did not provide an inventory gain estimate and will come back on that later.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 9% volume growth came from tyre and non-tyre?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was skewed towards tyres, with a lower contribution from non-tyre.

qa_highlights.question: Will the TDQ plant generate revenue this year, and at what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, revenue is expected this year. Non-tyre customers come first, followed by tyre companies over the next couple of quarters as approvals come through. No utilisation figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why might the Pilflex 13 ADD be approved this time when it was rejected in 2021?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Central Government has discretion, with a decision expected within about 90 days, possibly by end-September. It argued that domestic producers are under more stress now, so the case is stronger.

risks_watch: Central Government decision on Pilflex 13 ADD, expected around end-September; earlier 2021 DGTR recommendation was rejected.
Pass-through and sustainability of price gains: management expects moderation from Q1 realisation levels.
Antioxidant import pressure and falling YoY realisations, with no ADD approved on the antioxidant (TDQ) product.
Utility and gas availability, plus freight costs linked to the Middle East conflict, which may keep conversion costs high.
Pace of TDQ approvals by tyre customers, and whether Q4 FY27 volume reaches the 160-165 index level discussed by an analyst.
Raw material price volatility from the geopolitical situation.
Non-tyre demand recovery after temporary contraction.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the full-year outlook, but cautious on near-term costs and volumes. Management was evasive on quantifying ADD benefits, inventory gains, one-off costs and the Pilflex 13 outcome, and declined to comment on promoter pledging.
key_quotes: We expect revenue for Financial Year ‘27 to be in the range of Rs 1,400 to Rs 1,600 crores, based on the current pricing environment, with EBITDA in the region of 10%.
